beforeTrip.title: What to know before you go
beforeTrip.intro: Double-check documents, money, connectivity, and packing before departure. (For apps, see the Useful Apps menu.)
beforeTrip.docs1: Make sure your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond your return date. Depending on nationality you may need a visa or electronic travel authorization — check official guidance before you fly.
beforeTrip.docs2: Immigration may ask for your hotel address and purpose of stay. Keep a booking confirmation or address ready on your phone.
beforeTrip.docs3: Travel insurance is strongly recommended for medical costs, lost items, and flight delays.
beforeTrip.money1: Cards are widely accepted, but markets, stalls, and some small shops/taxis may want cash. Carry a little won (about ₩50,000–100,000).
beforeTrip.money2: Compare airport exchange, city exchangers, and ATMs. Check your card’s foreign-transaction fees in advance.
beforeTrip.money3: Buy and top up a T-money/Cashbee transit card at a convenience store or subway station on day one.
beforeTrip.connect1: Get an eSIM or physical SIM at the airport or online. Relying only on free Wi-Fi can cut off maps and translation.
beforeTrip.connect2: Korea uses 220V with Type C/F plugs. Bring an adapter if your devices use Type A only.
beforeTrip.connect3: A power bank and multi-adapter make all-day maps and photos much easier.
beforeTrip.pack1: Pack for the season and bring comfortable shoes — Seoul involves a lot of walking. Summers are humid; winters are cold and windy.
beforeTrip.pack2: Book stays early for peak seasons and holidays. Note check-in time, luggage storage, and English support.
beforeTrip.pack3: Bring basic meds you trust, toiletries, and a few spare masks. Convenience stores sell many items, but familiar medicine is easier.

emergency.title: Emergency Information
emergency.desc: In an emergency, call 112 (police) or 119 (fire/ambulance). For tourist interpretation help, call 1330.

kimbap.title: Kimbap
kimbap.desc: Rice and fillings rolled in seaweed
kimbap.about: Kimbap is a Korean dish made by rolling rice and various fillings in seaweed. It is easy to eat, and each restaurant offers different ingredients and flavors.

naengmyeon.title: Naengmyeon
naengmyeon.about: Naengmyeon is a Korean cold noodle dish.

jeon.title: Jeon
jeon.about: Jeon is a savory Korean pancake made with batter and various ingredients.

jajangmyeon.title: Jajangmyeon
jajangmyeon.about: Jajangmyeon is noodles mixed with black bean sauce.

dakhanmari.title: Dak Hanmari
dakhanmari.about: Dak Hanmari is a hot pot made with a whole chicken.

budae-jjigae.title: Budae Jjigae
budae-jjigae.desc: Stew with sausage, ham and kimchi
budae-jjigae.about: Budae Jjigae is a stew with sausage, ham, and kimchi.

dakgalbi.title: Dakgalbi
dakgalbi.about: Dakgalbi is spicy stir-fried chicken and vegetables.

samgyetang.title: Samgyetang
samgyetang.about: Samgyetang is ginseng chicken soup with glutinous rice.

bibimbap.title: Bibimbap
bibimbap.desc: Mixed rice with vegetables and chili paste
bibimbap.about: Bibimbap is mixed rice with vegetables and chili paste.

ganjang-gejang.title: Ganjang Gejang
ganjang-gejang.about: Ganjang Gejang is raw crab marinated in soy sauce.

yangnyeom-chicken.title: Yangnyeom Chicken
yangnyeom-chicken.desc: Sweet and spicy Korean fried chicken
yangnyeom-chicken.about: Yangnyeom chicken is fried chicken coated in a sweet and spicy sauce.

sundubu-jjigae.title: Sundubu Jjigae
sundubu-jjigae.about: Sundubu-jjigae is a spicy soft-tofu stew. Crack an egg into the bubbling pot and eat with rice and kimchi — an easy Korean classic for visitors.

sulbing.title: Sulbing
sulbing.about: Sulbing is an easy-to-find Korean bingsu brand known for injeolmi (soybean powder) shaved ice.

paris-baguette.title: Paris Baguette
paris-baguette.about: One of Korea’s most common bakery chains — bread, cakes, and coffee in one stop.

tous-les-jours.title: Tous Les Jours
tous-les-jours.desc: Bakery brand with soft breads and cakes
tous-les-jours.about: Tous Les Jours is known for soft milk breads and dessert pastries.

jjimdak.title: Jjimdak
jjimdak.desc: Sweet-spicy braised chicken with glass noodles
jjimdak.about: Jjimdak is chicken braised with potato, carrot, and glass noodles in a sweet-spicy soy/gochujang sauce. Andong jjimdak is the famous style — great for sharing.

bingsu.title: Bingsu
bingsu.about: Bingsu is finely shaved milk ice or ice topped with red beans, fruit, rice cake, and ice cream. Especially popular in summer at dessert cafés and chains.

bread.title: Bread · Bakery
bread.desc: Korean bakery chains and popular breads
bread.about: Korea has bakery chains like Paris Baguette and Tous Les Jours nationwide — from meal breads to sweet pastries.

cafe.title: Café
cafe.about: Korea has everything from value takeout coffee shops to café chains with desserts and light meals. You’ll find them near tourist spots and subway stations — handy for a break while traveling.

malatang.title: Malatang
malatang.about: Malatang is a spicy hot-pot-style soup popular with young locals and travelers. Pick ingredients (veggies, noodles, meat, tofu), choose a spice level and broth, then simmer and eat.

tteokbokki.title: Tteokbokki
tteokbokki.desc: Chewy rice cakes in sweet-spicy sauce
tteokbokki.about: Tteokbokki is Korea’s classic street snack: chewy rice cakes simmered in a gochujang sauce. You’ll find it at street stalls, snack shops, and convenience stores — plus cheese, rose, and soup styles.

nangman-sandwich.title: Nangman sandwich
nangman-sandwich.about: “Nangman sandwich” (romantic sandwich) is a viral thick-sandwich trend. Layers of egg, ham, veggies, and sauce make a photogenic cross-section — popular at cafés and bakeries as a meal or sweet-savory treat.

dubai-cookie.title: Dubai chewy cookie
dubai-cookie.desc: Chewy chocolate cookie with pistachio & kadaif
dubai-cookie.about: Inspired by viral Dubai-style chocolate, these chewy cookies or chocolate treats layer pistachio cream and crunchy kadaif (shredded pastry). Often sold as seasonal specials at bakeries and dessert shops.

butter-bread.title: Butter bread
butter-bread.desc: Rich bakery bread loaded with butter
butter-bread.about: Butter bread is a Korean bakery favorite: soft bread filled or topped with generous butter (or butter cream). Best warm when the butter melts — a signature at many famous bakeries and chains.

tanghulu.title: Tanghulu
tanghulu.desc: Fruit skewers with a crunchy sugar shell
tanghulu.about: Tanghulu is candied fruit on a stick (strawberry, shine muscat, etc.) with a crunchy sugar coating. It became a trendy street dessert in Korea too — quite sweet, so one or two skewers is usually enough.

yogurt-ice.title: Yogurt ice cream
yogurt-ice.about: Yogurt ice cream (soft serve) is popular for its tangy, lighter taste. Add fruit, cereal, or toppings — easy to find at chain dessert shops near tourist areas.

bungeoppang.title: Bungeoppang
bungeoppang.desc: Fish-shaped street pastry, often filled with red bean
bungeoppang.about: Bungeoppang is a fish-shaped pastry cooked in a mold, usually filled with sweet red bean (also cream or savory versions). A classic winter street snack — best eaten hot from the stall.

wonjo-nude-cheese.name: Wonjo Nude Cheese Kimbap No.41
wonjo-nude-cheese.location: 88 Changgyeonggung-ro (Gwangjang Market Stall No.41), Jongno-gu, Seoul
wonjo-nude-cheese.tip: Inside Gwangjang Market alleys. Nude style has no outer seaweed wrap; japchae kimbap is also popular.
wonjo-nude-cheese.about: A Gwangjang Market classic known for nude and japchae kimbap.

oto.name: Oto Kimbap
oto.tip: Clear wasabi kick — ask for milder if needed.
oto.about: Specialty kimbap with a wasabi accent.

horangi.name: Horangi Kimbap
horangi.tip: Hearty premium bulgogi filling. Use a map app in Seongbuk-dong.

food2900.name: FOOD 2900
food2900.tip: Budget-friendly sausage kimbap near Apgujeong Rodeo.
food2900.about: Value kimbap spot in Apgujeong Rodeo.

sua-dang.name: Sua-dang
sua-dang.tip: Lower-rice keto-style tuna roll near Dongseon-dong / Sungshin area.

owolui-kimbap.name: Owolui Kimbap
owolui-kimbap.tip: Loaded with egg — look for it along Bongcheon-ro in Gwanak-gu.

seoho.name: Seoho Kimbap
seoho.tip: Wrapped with kelp instead of regular gim — different aroma and bite.

hanipsoban.name: Hanip Soban
hanipsoban.menu: Aged kimchi kimbap, pork belly kimbap
hanipsoban.tip: Walkable from Sookmyung Women’s University Station.
hanipsoban.about: Popular for aged-kimchi and samgyeopsal kimbap.

sulbing.name: Sulbing
sulbing.tip: Seasonal menus rotate often. Some shops have kiosk/app ordering.
sulbing.about: Sulbing’s signature is injeolmi bingsu with soybean powder, rice cake, red bean, and ice cream.

paris-baguette.name: Paris Baguette
paris-baguette.location: Near stations and shopping streets nationwide
paris-baguette.menu: Garlic baguette, sandwiches, cakes, and more
paris-baguette.tip: Handy for quick breakfasts and lunches. Stock differs by store.
paris-baguette.about: A convenient bakery stop while traveling — garlic bread and cream-cheese items are popular.

tous-les-jours.name: Tous Les Jours
tous-les-jours.menu: Milk bread, pastries, cakes, and more
tous-les-jours.tip: Soft breads pair well with coffee to take back to your stay.
tous-les-jours.about: Typical Tous Les Jours picks: soft breads and sweet pastries.

mega-coffee.name: Mega Coffee
mega-coffee.location: Major shopping areas & near stations nationwide
mega-coffee.tip: Many shops are takeout-focused. Check app coupons and size-up deals.
mega-coffee.about: A value coffee chain popular across Korea. Easy to find near tourist areas when you want a quick cup.

starbucks.name: Starbucks
starbucks.location: Nationwide (many tourist spots: Myeongdong, Gangnam, airports)
starbucks.tip: Many stores have Wi‑Fi and outlets for a short break. Seasonal merch sells out fast at busy shops.
starbucks.about: One of the most common café brands in Korea. Familiar for international travelers, with easy card/app payment.

compose-coffee.name: Compose Coffee
compose-coffee.tip: Mostly takeout. Ask about bean options or extra shots to adjust the taste.
compose-coffee.about: A budget-friendly coffee brand popular with locals. Great for a quick takeaway while sightseeing.

ediya.name: Ediya Coffee
ediya.tip: Many shops have seats for a short rest. Ask for decaf or sweetness adjustments.
ediya.about: A large Korean café chain. Easy to grab coffee plus a simple bakery item.

twosome-place.name: A Twosome Place
twosome-place.menu: Cakes & desserts, coffee, light brunch items
twosome-place.tip: Great for cake + coffee. Whole cakes may need advance order.
twosome-place.about: A dessert-forward café brand. Popular for celebrations and a sit-down coffee break.

paiks-coffee.name: Paik’s Coffee
paiks-coffee.tip: “Original coffee” is on the sweet side. Choose Americano or ask to reduce sweetness if you prefer less sugar.
paiks-coffee.about: A budget coffee brand linked to chef Baek Jong-won, known for sweet signature drinks and affordable prices.

yoajeong.name: Yoajeong
yoajeong.tip: Too many toppings can get heavy. Use takeout if the line is long.
yoajeong.about: Yoajeong is a popular yogurt soft-serve brand. People love the tangy base plus creative topping mixes.

tips.mapMistake: Coming to Korea with only Google Maps
tips.mapBody: When traveling in Korea, install Naver Map or Kakao Map in addition to Google Maps. For public transit, walking directions, and local shop info, Naver Map and Kakao Map are often more accurate.
tips.cardMistake: Buying a ticket every time, or not tapping out on the bus
tips.cardBody: A transit card is useful not only for buses and the subway, but also for taxis and public bikes. You can buy and top up cards at convenience stores or subway stations. One thing many travelers miss: on buses, you must tap your card again when you get off.
tips.restaurantMistake: Assuming restaurants work the same as abroad
tips.restaurantBody1: You might wait for staff to take your order when there is a call bell at the table, or ask for water and side dishes when there is a self-service station. More places now use kiosks or tablets for ordering, which can be another hurdle if you do not read Korean.
tips.restaurantBody2: Some visitors also think they should leave a tip in Korea, leaving cash on the table or looking for a way to add tip on a card payment. Tipping is not common at typical Korean restaurants.
tips.restaurantBody3: Abroad, staff often bring the bill to your table. In many Korean restaurants, you finish eating and then pay at the counter near the entrance.
tips.cashBody: Most places take cards, but traditional markets, street stalls, and some small restaurants/taxis are cash-only. Keep small bills.
tips.trashBody: Public bins are fewer than many visitors expect. Use convenience stores, stations, or cafés — or take small trash back to your hotel.
tips.wifiBody: Public Wi-Fi can be unstable. An eSIM/SIM keeps maps, translation, and payment apps online.
tips.queueMistake: Sitting down without checking the queue
tips.queueBody: Popular restaurants often use waiting apps or number tickets at the door. If staff say “one moment,” check the line first.
tips.waterMistake: Waiting for staff to bring everything
tips.waterBody: Many places have a self-serve station for water, utensils, and banchan. Look around once you sit.
tips.rushBody: Weekdays 7–9 a.m. and 6–8 p.m. are packed. Avoid those times if you can, or take a taxi with heavy bags.
tips.taxiMistake: Only explaining the address out loud
tips.taxiBody: Use Kakao T / Uber-style apps, or show the destination in Korean. Ask for a receipt if you need one.
tips.exitBody: Exit numbers matter a lot. Check the recommended exit in your map app before you leave the station.
tips.weekendMistake: Assuming weekend hotel rates match weekdays
tips.weekendBody: Friday–Sunday and holidays often cost much more than weekdays. Mix in weekday stays when you can, and compare prices early on booking apps. Same-day bookings can be pricier.

transport.mapCaption: Full network map · zoom in to explore
transport.tabsHelp: Tap a tab to view details.
transport.subwayIntro: Each Seoul Metro line has its own color. Station names and transfer signs appear in Korean, English, Japanese, and Chinese. A T-money card is the easiest way to ride buses and the subway.
transport.officialMapDesc: For the most accurate official diagram, open Seoul Metro Cyber Station. Embedding it here is blocked by the site’s policy.
transport.interactiveMapHelp: Tap a line button to highlight that route on the map. (Based on real track geometry — the layout differs from the schematic diagram.)
transport.linePickHint: Choose a line to highlight it on the map and show a short description below.
transport.subwayTip1: Buy and top up T-money at convenience stores or subway stations.
transport.subwayTip2: Rush hours (weekdays 7–9 a.m., 6–8 p.m.) are very crowded.
transport.subwayTip3: Use Kakao Map or Naver Map for live directions.
transport.line1Desc: A north–south line through Seoul Station, Jongno, and Dongdaemun. It also connects toward Incheon and Suwon.
transport.line1Stops: Key stops: Seoul Station · City Hall · Jonggak · Jongno 3-ga · Dongdaemun
transport.line2Desc: A loop line around Seoul. One of the most useful lines for travelers.
transport.line2Stops: Key stops: Hongik Univ. · City Hall · Dongdaemun History & Culture Park · Jamsil · Gangnam · Sadang
transport.line3Desc: Connects palaces, Apgujeong, and Express Bus Terminal. Handy for Gyeongbokgung and Anguk.
transport.line3Stops: Key stops: Gyeongbokgung · Anguk · Jongno 3-ga · Apgujeong · Express Bus Terminal · Gyodae
transport.line4Desc: Runs through Myeongdong, Seoul Station, and Hyehwa. Great for shopping and Namsan access.
transport.line4Stops: Key stops: Seoul Station · Myeongdong · Chungmuro · Hyehwa · Suyu · Sadang
transport.line5Desc: Crosses Yeouido, Gwanghwamun, and Dongdaemun, linking south and north of the Han River.
transport.line5Stops: Key stops: Yeouido · Gwanghwamun · Jongno 3-ga · Dongdaemun History & Culture Park · Wangsimni
transport.line6Desc: Serves Itaewon, Hannam, and Gongdeok—popular areas with many international visitors.
transport.line6Stops: Key stops: Gongdeok · Samgakji · Itaewon · Hangangjin · Yaksu · Dongmyo
transport.line7Desc: Links Express Bus Terminal, Konkuk Univ., and Nowon. Useful around Gangnam and Konkuk.
transport.line7Stops: Key stops: Express Bus Terminal · Nonhyeon · Gangnam-gu Office · Konkuk Univ. · Nowon
transport.line9Desc: Runs from Gimpo Airport through Yeouido and Sinnonhyeon, with express trains.
transport.line9Stops: Key stops: Gimpo Airport · Yeouido · Noryangjin · Sinnonhyeon · Bongeunsa · Sports Complex
transport.arexDesc: Connects Incheon Airport and Seoul Station. Express (~43 min) and all-stop (~60 min) trains are available.
transport.arexStops: Key stops: Incheon Airport T1/T2 · Hongik Univ. · Gongdeok · Seoul Station
transport.routeIntro: Step-by-step routes to popular places. Times vary with transfers and walking — double-check in Kakao Map or Naver Map before you go.
transport.route_amd_s1: From Incheon Airport T1/T2, follow signs for AREX to the underground platforms. Use elevators if you have a large suitcase.
transport.route_amd_s2: Buy/ride the All-Stop train (not Express unless you specifically want Seoul Station only). Express is pricier and skips most stops.
transport.route_amd_s3: Ride to Seoul Station (about 50–60 min). Watch the display for the next stops and get off at Seoul Station.
transport.route_ahd_s1: At Incheon Airport, find the AREX All-Stop platform (both terminals connect to AREX).
transport.route_ahd_s2: Ride to Hongik Univ. Station — no transfer, one of the easiest first-day routes.
transport.route_ahd_s3: Move toward the doors when Hongik Univ. appears on the display; stops are short.
transport.route_agn_s1: Take AREX All-Stop from the airport. Express only goes to Seoul Station, so All-Stop is usually better for Gangnam.
transport.route_agn_s2: Recommended: get off at Hongik Univ. → transfer to Line 2 toward Gangnam (check the board for direction).
transport.route_agn_s3: Line 2 is a loop — confirm you’re on the correct direction so Gangnam is upcoming.
transport.route_sgb_s1: Enter Seoul Station subway area (transfers from KTX/AREX can be a long walk).
transport.route_sgb_s2: Use your map app to Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3). It will suggest the simplest transfer from Line 1/4.
transport.route_sgb_s3: Exit 5 is convenient for the palace / Gwanghwamun side — a few minutes on foot.
transport.route_mhd_s1: Board at Myeongdong (Line 4). Avoid rush hour if you have big shopping bags.
transport.route_mhd_s2: Example: Myeongdong → (Line 4) → Dongdaemun History & Culture Park → (Line 2) → Hongik Univ.
transport.route_mhd_s3: Another option transfers via City Hall to Line 2. Use the map app for the faster option that day.
transport.route_mgn_s1: From Myeongdong (Line 4), ride one stop to Chungmuro.
transport.route_mgn_s3: Ride to Gyodae, transfer to Line 2, then one stop to Gangnam.
transport.route_hit_s1: From Hongik Univ., head toward Gongdeuk (AREX/Line 2 options — check the app).
transport.route_hit_s3: Get off at Itaewon. Exits 1–4 are usually closest to the main street.
transport.route_amd_s4: Transfer to subway Line 4 (blue). Follow transfer signs; toward Sadang/Namtaeryeong is the Myeongdong direction.
transport.route_amd_s5: Get off at Myeongdong. Exits 6–8 are often best for the shopping street; confirm the recommended exit in your map app.
transport.route_amd_tip: Airport buses are an option with very heavy luggage. Keep big bags near the doors/luggage space on AREX.
transport.route_ahd_s4: Exits 9 and 1 are often closest to the main nightlife streets — check your hotel’s exit number.
transport.route_ahd_s5: Late at night the area is crowded and alleys are confusing; walking or a short taxi to your stay is fine.
transport.route_ahd_tip: Hongik Univ. is a big transfer hub (AREX / Line 2 / Gyeongui–Jungang). Wrong exits can add 10+ minutes.
transport.route_agn_s4: Get off at Gangnam. Exits 11–12 are famous for the main strip, but your hotel may need another exit.
transport.route_agn_s5: Alternatives: AREX to Seoul Station then bus, or an airport bus with a seat if you have lots of luggage.
transport.route_agn_tip: Line 2 around Gangnam is very crowded at rush hour. Keep suitcases by the doors, not in the aisle.
transport.route_sgb_s4: Check closed days (often Mondays) and ticket options before you go.
transport.route_sgb_s5: Bring a hat/umbrella for heat or rain while walking the grounds.
transport.route_sgb_tip: Hanbok rental is popular nearby. A small bag makes entry easier.
transport.route_mhd_s4: At Hongik Univ., pick the exit for Hongdae streets / Yeonnam-dong as needed.
transport.route_mhd_s5: Evenings are packed — meet friends by exit number.
transport.route_mhd_tip: It may feel walkable on a map, but the subway is usually faster and easier.
transport.route_mgn_s4: Exit using the map app’s recommendation for your exact destination.
transport.route_mgn_s5: Buses work too when traveling light, but subway is clearer for first-timers.
transport.route_mgn_tip: Chungmuro and Gyodae transfers are relatively short.
transport.route_hit_s4: Hills and alleys can be tiring with luggage — consider a short taxi at night.
transport.route_hit_s5: Weekends are crowded; keep valuables in front.
transport.route_hit_tip: Some routes transfer at Hapjeong — follow whichever the map says is faster live.
transport.placesIntro: Pick a region, then browse popular places with short how-to-get tips.
transport.place_myeongdong_desc: Seoul’s classic shopping and street-food district with duty-free stores.
transport.place_myeongdong_how: Line 4 Myeongdong Station. Exits 1 and 6–8 are closest to the main street.
transport.place_gyeongbok_desc: Joseon’s main palace — pair with hanbok rental and the palace museum.
transport.place_gyeongbok_how: Line 3 Gyeongbokgung Station exit 5. Also walkable from Gwanghwamun/Anguk.
transport.place_gangnam_desc: Shopping, cafés, nightlife — often includes Gangnam Station, Sinnonhyeon, Garosu-gil, Apgujeong.
transport.place_gangnam_how: Line 2 / Shinbundang Gangnam Station; exits 11–12 for the busy side.
transport.place_hongdae_desc: Youth culture, busking, cafés, clubs — especially lively at night.
transport.place_hongdae_how: Line 2 / AREX / Gyeongui–Jungang Hongik Univ. Station; exits 9 and 1.
transport.place_itaewon_desc: International food and bars; connects toward Haebangchon and Gyeongnidan.
transport.place_suwon_desc: UNESCO fortress walls and Hwaseong Haenggung palace.
transport.place_suwon_how: Line 1 Suwon Station then bus/taxi, or check Suin–Bundang walking routes.
transport.place_goyang_desc: Large park for cycling, picnics, and evening lights.
transport.place_goyang_how: Line 3 Madu / Jeongbalsan area — check lake-park exits on the map.
transport.place_gapyeong_desc: Nami Island and nearby day-trip spots in northeast Gyeonggi.
transport.place_gapyeong_how: Gyeongchun Line Gapyeong / Nami Island (Gyeonggang) Station; ITX also runs.
transport.place_haeundae_desc: Busan’s famous beach with Dongbaek Island and Marine City nearby.
transport.place_haeundae_how: Busan Metro Line 2 Haeundae Station; short walk or bus to the sand.
transport.place_nampo_desc: Jagalchi fish market, Gukje Market, and BIFF Square eats.
transport.place_seomyeon_desc: Busan’s central shopping and transfer hub.

apps.kakaoDesc: Strong for directions, transit, and taxis. Shop info is usually accurate because locals use it heavily.
apps.naverDesc: Detailed subway/bus transfers and live arrivals. Great walking routes too.
apps.papagoDesc: Korean↔English/Japanese translation plus photo text recognition — perfect for menus.
apps.talkDesc: Korea’s main messenger. Needed for hotels, tours, and adding local contacts.
apps.yanoljaDesc: Hotels, motels, and guesthouses with frequent same-day deals.
apps.yeogiDesc: Easy stay comparison and reviews. Photos and maps help even if the UI is Korean.
apps.coupangDesc: Groceries and food delivery. Often accepts foreign cards — handy for short stays.
apps.tmoneyDesc: Check transit card balance/top-up and some mobility services in one app.

souvenir.maskDesc: Cheap at convenience stores, Daiso, and Olive Young — popular emergency travel buys.
souvenir.stationeryDesc: Daiso, Artbox, and Kakao Friends stationery are light and gift-friendly.
souvenir.oliveDesc: Lip balm, hand cream, and travel kits (“Olive Young picks”) are common souvenirs.
souvenir.daisoDesc: Household and character goods at low prices — easy to fit in a suitcase.
souvenir.snackDesc: Pepero, Honey Butter Chips, and jelly packs from marts/convenience stores are classic gifts.
souvenir.ramenDesc: Buldak, chapagetti, and cup noodle sets are high satisfaction for the weight.
souvenir.teaDesc: Ginseng tea, yuja tea, and tea-bag sets are easy to find and nicely packaged.
souvenir.honeyDesc: Traditional sweet sets sell well at airports and markets — pack carefully so they don’t crush.
souvenir.uniqloDesc: Korea-only colors and character collab tees are popular keepsakes.
souvenir.spaDesc: Spao, Mixxo, and 8Seconds are common stops for budget casual wear.
souvenir.socksDesc: Character sock sets are light, cheap, and hard to get wrong as gifts.
souvenir.hanbokDesc: Besides rentals, norigae charms, handkerchiefs, and mini keyrings sell well.
souvenir.sheetDesc: Box sets (Mediheal, numbuzin, etc.) are among the top beauty gifts.
souvenir.sunscreenDesc: Lightweight Korean sunscreens get repurchase love — mind airline liquid limits.
souvenir.lipstickDesc: Rom&nd / Peripera tints and cushion compacts are compact gift favorites.
souvenir.kpopDesc: Albums, light sticks, Kakao Friends, and Line Friends toys are easy to find in Myeongdong, Hongdae, and airports.
souvenir.tapHint: Tap a card for where to buy and practical tips.
souvenir.maskBody1: Many travelers pick up KF94/KF80 masks for dust season or colds. Convenience stores, Daiso, Olive Young, and pharmacies all stock them; small multi-packs pack easier than singles.
souvenir.maskBody2: Hand sanitizer is handy on subways, buses, and in restaurants early in the trip. Choose travel sizes under airline liquid limits (usually 100 ml).
souvenir.maskTip: Neighborhood Daiso or convenience stores are often cheaper than tourist Olive Young shops. Buy early so you can actually use them.
souvenir.stationeryBody1: Korean stationery is known for design and value. Daiso basics, Artbox/Alpha notebooks and stickers, and Kakao/Line Friends character goods make easy gifts.
souvenir.stationeryBody2: Stickers, washi tape, and mini notebooks are light and compact — perfect when suitcase space is tight or you need many small presents.
souvenir.stationeryTip: Stationery clusters near Myeongdong, Hongdae, and Gangnam underground malls. In Daiso, hunt the dedicated stationery aisle — stock differs by floor.
souvenir.oliveBody1: Olive Young feels like a souvenir shop for many visitors. Lip balm, hand cream, travel kits, and Olive Young pick bundles are common keepsakes.
souvenir.oliveBody2: Signature brand walls (Round Lab, Anua, Mediheal, etc.) show what locals buy. You can also ask staff for tourist favorites.
souvenir.oliveTip: Airport and hotspot stores sell out fast. Large city stores (Myeongdong, Gangnam, Hongdae) are easier. Confirm tax-free before checkout.
souvenir.daisoBody1: Daiso is Korea’s go-to variety store — kitchen tools, organizers, character goods, and simple beauty tools in one place, often at fixed low prices.
souvenir.daisoBody2: Small cutting boards, tongs, eco bags, and cable organizers are practical souvenirs. Ask for extra packing for glass or ceramics.
souvenir.daisoTip: Tourist-area Daiso can be crowded; residential branches are calmer. Recheck weight and bulk before you pay.
souvenir.snackBody1: Snacks and jelly are low-risk classics: Pepero, Honey Butter Chips, shrimp crackers, and candy packs are everywhere in marts and convenience stores.
souvenir.snackBody2: For gifts, choose individually wrapped items or gift packs. In summer, watch melting chocolate.
souvenir.snackTip: Hypermarket promo aisles often beat convenience-store prices. Buying the day before departure makes packing easier.
souvenir.ramenBody1: Buldak, chapagetti, neoguri, and cup-noodle multipacks are top edible souvenirs — high satisfaction for the weight. Marts/Daiso usually beat convenience stores on multipacks.
souvenir.ramenBody2: Hetbahn rice packs pair well for easy Korean meals at home. Bag liquid soup packets in zip bags so they do not burst under pressure.
souvenir.ramenTip: Customs rules vary: check meat/agriculture restrictions and ingredient labels for your destination country.
souvenir.teaBody1: Ginseng tea, yuja tea, barley tea, and tea-bag sets are easy to find in department-store food halls, souvenir shops, and airports — packaging looks gift-ready.
souvenir.teaBody2: Yuja and honey-ginger often come as concentrated jars (liquids). Mind carry-on rules and cushion jars between clothes.
souvenir.teaTip: Duty-free/department sets cost more but look premium. Buy mart tea bags for yourself and sets for gifts to save money.
souvenir.honeyBody1: Yakgwa and hangwa feel distinctly Korean and sweet — popular edible souvenirs. Honey and grain syrup sets are often sold nearby.
souvenir.honeyBody2: Yakgwa crumbles easily; prefer boxed products with padding. Re-wrap loose market packs at your hotel.
souvenir.honeyTip: Incheon Airport traditional-food counters and Insadong/Gwangjang Market areas have wide selections. Check expiry and storage notes.
souvenir.uniqloBody1: Even global SPA brands stock Korea-only colors, graphics, and character collabs. Limited tees are a common only-in-Korea buy.
souvenir.uniqloBody2: Seasonal sales are competitive, and tax-free flows are familiar. Always try sizes in the fitting room.
souvenir.uniqloTip: Large stores (Myeongdong, Times Square, COEX) have better stock. Use cm on the label — Korean sizing varies by brand.
souvenir.spaBody1: Korean SPA brands like Spao, Mixxo, 8Seconds, and Topten offer trendy casual wear at fair prices — clothing that doubles as a souvenir.
souvenir.spaBody2: Character, variety-show, and idol collab tees plus light outerwear sell well. Prefer thin pieces to save luggage weight.
souvenir.spaTip: Stores cluster in Hongdae, Myeongdong, and Gangnam. Photo the return policy in case of issues after you fly home.
souvenir.socksBody1: Character socks, sleep socks, and sock sets are light, cheap, and hard to get wrong as bulk gifts. Find them at Daiso, sock shops, and SPA brands.
souvenir.socksBody2: Underwear and tights are also useful mid-trip. For gifts, pick individually packed sets.
souvenir.socksTip: 3- or 5-pair packs beat singles on value and slip into suitcase gaps.
souvenir.hanbokBody1: Besides palace rental hanbok, modern hanbok-style tops, norigae charms, handkerchiefs, and mini keyrings make portable cultural souvenirs.
souvenir.hanbokBody2: Tourist-shop prices vary widely — compare Insadong, Tongin Market, and department-store traditional corners. Check fabric and stitching by hand.
souvenir.hanbokTip: Rent for photos; buy small accessories to take home. Full hanbok is bulky and wrinkles in a suitcase.
souvenir.sheetBody1: Sheet-mask box sets are the classic K-beauty souvenir. Familiar Olive Young / duty-free names (Mediheal, numbuzin, TIRTIR, etc.) are safer picks.
souvenir.sheetBody2: Around 10 sheets per box works for gifts and personal use. Patch-test if you react to fragrance, retinol, or acids.
souvenir.sheetTip: Olive Young sale periods improve value. Pack liquid-heavy boxes in checked luggage.
souvenir.sunscreenBody1: Lightweight Korean sunscreens and tone-up suns often become repurchase favorites. Check chemical vs mineral filters, white cast, and tone-up on the label.
souvenir.sunscreenBody2: Travel sizes, cushions, and sticks are easier under liquid rules. Note the use-by period after opening.
souvenir.sunscreenTip: Popular SKUs sell out in peak seasons. Two bottles under 100 ml can be easier for carry-on than one large bottle.
souvenir.lipstickBody1: Rom&nd, Peripera, Clio tints and cushions are compact gift favorites. Always swatch testers in store.
souvenir.lipstickBody2: For cushions, check shade and refill options; for tints, dryness and stay-power. Sets often beat singles during sales.
souvenir.lipstickTip: Staff can help match undertones — ask for a natural or vivid look in simple words.
souvenir.kpopBody1: Albums, photocards, light sticks, official MD, and Kakao/Line Friends plush are easy to find in Myeongdong, Hongdae, Gangnam, and airports.
souvenir.kpopBody2: Official or licensed stores are safer for authenticity. Extremely cheap street goods may be fakes.
souvenir.kpopTip: Light sticks and figures are bulky — leave suitcase space, or bring a compression pouch instead of relying on shopping bags.

convenience.intro: Korean convenience-store ‘honey combos’ went viral on SNS and TV. Most need only a microwave.
convenience.c1Desc: Mix Chapagetti jjajang cup + spicy jjamppong cup
convenience.c2Desc: Cup tteokbokki + spaghetti ramyeon + sausage + cheese
convenience.c3Desc: Carbonara Buldak noodles + tuna-mayo triangle kimbap
convenience.c5Desc: Kaguri curry udon + grilled chicken + cheese
convenience.c6Desc: Dip Melona ice cream in iced coffee
convenience.c1_lead: The classic convenience-store drink hack. Mixing sweet banana milk with bitter coffee turns it into a dessert drink.
convenience.c1_products: Binggrae banana milk (or similar) · iced Americano (cup/can) from CU/GS25/7-Eleven · optional straw
convenience.c1_s1: Pick chilled banana milk and an iced Americano (or canned Americano).
convenience.c1_s2: Pour coffee into the banana milk little by little — start with 1/3 to 1/2 and adjust to taste.
convenience.c1_s3: Shake or stir. Add more coffee if too sweet, keep more milk if too bitter.
convenience.c1_tip: You can also pour banana milk into the coffee cup. Choose low-fat banana milk if you want it lighter.
convenience.c2_lead: A reliable light meal. Triangle kimbap comes in many fillings — pick your favorite.
convenience.c2_products: Triangle kimbap (tuna mayo, kimchi, spicy, etc.) · banana milk · optional wet wipes
convenience.c2_s1: Peel the wrapper following the 1 → 2 → 3 marks. Open just before eating so the seaweed stays crisp.
convenience.c2_s2: Bite so seaweed, rice, and filling come together; sip banana milk between bites.
convenience.c2_s3: Spicy fillings pair especially well with the sweet milk. Add an egg or hot bar if you want more.
convenience.c2_tip: Popular fillings sell out morning/late night. Check the expiry date and only microwave labeled products.
convenience.c3_lead: A popular upgrade that makes cup noodles much more filling — especially with spicy noodles.
convenience.c3_products: Cup ramyeon · boiled egg · 1 slice of cheese · chopsticks and hot water
convenience.c3_s1: Add hot water and wait as directed (use less water for stir-fry style noodles).
convenience.c3_s2: Add halved egg and a cheese slice on top; cover briefly so the cheese melts.
convenience.c3_s3: Stir lightly so the cheese melts into the broth, then eat right away.
convenience.c3_tip: Some eggs can be warmed in the store microwave. Watch for spills.
convenience.c4_lead: Crispy honey cookies with bitter coffee — a Korean tea-time combo from the convenience store.
convenience.c4_products: Yakgwa (individually wrapped or mini) · iced/hot Americano or latte
convenience.c4_s1: Open the yakgwa carefully — it can crumble.
convenience.c4_s2: Alternate bites of yakgwa with sips of coffee.
convenience.c4_s3: Latte for sweeter pairing, Americano for a cleaner finish.
convenience.c4_tip: Yakgwa is rich in oil and sugar — check the date and don’t leave it in heat too long.
convenience.c5_lead: Easy ‘chimaek’ vibes at your stay. Heat per package directions.
convenience.c5_products: Convenience fried/seasoned chicken · beer or non-alcoholic beer · optional pickles and wipes
convenience.c5_s1: Follow microwave wattage/time on the package (and thawing steps if frozen).
convenience.c5_s2: For crispier texture, vent the cover briefly or use an air fryer if available.
convenience.c5_s3: Eat with beer right away. Keep wipes ready for saucy chicken.
convenience.c5_tip: Alcohol purchase has age limits. Respect lodging rules for smell and trash sorting.
convenience.c6_lead: Dip Melona into coffee (or eat them together) for a sweet dessert — a summer photo favorite.
convenience.c6_products: Melona bar · iced Americano or unsweetened iced coffee · optional straw
convenience.c6_s1: Unwrap Melona and open the iced coffee lid.
convenience.c6_s2: Dip the tip of the Melona into the coffee and eat as it melts.
convenience.c6_s3: If it melts too fast, alternate bites outdoors in the shade.
convenience.c6_tip: It’s quite sweet — best as a dessert. Melona melts quickly in heat.
convenience.tapHint: Tap a card for ingredients and steps.
convenience.gongganchunDesc: Mix Chapagetti jjajang cup + spicy jjamppong cup
convenience.markjeongsikDesc: Cup tteokbokki + spaghetti ramyeon + sausage + cheese
convenience.carbonaraDesc: Carbonara Buldak noodles + tuna-mayo triangle kimbap
convenience.jikgguriDesc: Kaguri curry udon + grilled chicken + cheese
convenience.melonaDesc: Dip Melona ice cream in iced coffee
convenience.gongganchun_lead: Mix jjajang cup noodles with spicy jjamppong cup noodles for savory-spicy flavor.
convenience.gongganchun_products: 1 Chapagetti/jjajang cup, 1 spicy seafood jjamppong cup. Optional cheese/egg.
convenience.gongganchun_s1: Cook both noodles (use about one cup of water total in a larger bowl if needed).
convenience.gongganchun_s3: Add water if too salty; more jjamppong powder if you want more heat.
convenience.gongganchun_tip: Brand names vary — any jjajang cup + jjamppong cup works.
convenience.markjeongsik_lead: Viral fan recipe: cup tteokbokki with spaghetti ramyeon, sausage, and cheese.
convenience.markjeongsik_products: Cup tteokbokki, spaghetti-style cup noodles, sausage, 1–2 cheese slices.
convenience.markjeongsik_s1: Heat tteokbokki and cook spaghetti noodles.
convenience.markjeongsik_s2: Combine noodles in the tteokbokki cup; add sausage and cheese.
convenience.markjeongsik_s3: Microwave 20–40s to melt cheese, then mix.
convenience.markjeongsik_tip: Extra cheddar boosts flavor. Control spice with tteokbokki sauce.
convenience.carbonara_lead: Mix Carbonara Buldak with tuna-mayo kimbap rice for a creamy ‘risotto’.
convenience.carbonara_products: Carbonara Buldak noodles, tuna-mayo triangle kimbap. Optional cheese/milk.
convenience.carbonara_s2: Unwrap kimbap and add the rice to the noodles.
convenience.carbonara_s3: Mix into a risotto texture; add cheese/milk if dry.
convenience.carbonara_tip: Too spicy? Add more rice or use less chili powder.
convenience.eolbaksa_lead: Ice cup + Bacchus energy drink + lemon-lime soda — a refreshing pick-me-up.
convenience.eolbaksa_products: Ice cup, Bacchus (or similar), cider/Sprite-style soda.
convenience.eolbaksa_s1: Start with a cup of ice.
convenience.eolbaksa_s2: Pour Bacchus, then top with soda.
convenience.eolbaksa_s3: Stir and drink. Use more soda if too sweet.
convenience.eolbaksa_tip: Has caffeine and sugar — go easy at night.
convenience.jikgguri_lead: Kaguri curry-udon topped with grilled chicken and melted cheese.
convenience.jikgguri_products: Kaguri (curry udon), grilled chicken pack, cheese slice.
convenience.jikgguri_s2: Heat chicken and place on noodles.
convenience.jikgguri_tip: Pair with triangle kimbap. Chicken brand names vary by store.
convenience.melona_lead: Dip Melona in iced coffee or melt pieces into the cup.
convenience.melona_s2: Dip Melona or drop pieces into the cup.
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkisDesc: Mix blue lemonade with creamy Milkis soda
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_pageTitle: How to make Blue lemonade + Milkis
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_lead: A viral convenience-store drink mix: tangy blue lemonade plus creamy Milkis soda tastes like a café-style ade.
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_products: 1 blue lemonade (PET/can), 1 Milkis. Optional: ice cup & straw.
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_s1: Chill both drinks. Grab an ice cup if available.
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_s2: Pour blue lemonade about halfway into a cup, then slowly add Milkis (about 1:1).
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_s3: Stir lightly and drink. More lemonade = sharper; more Milkis = creamier.
convenience.blue-lemonade-milkis_tip: Pour slowly so the soda doesn’t overflow. Exact product names vary by store.
convenience.choco-banana-latteDesc: Mix banana milk first, then chocolate milk
convenience.choco-banana-latte_pageTitle: How to make Choco banana latte
convenience.choco-banana-latte_lead: Start with banana milk, then add chocolate milk for a café-style choco-banana drink — no coffee required.
convenience.choco-banana-latte_products: 1 banana milk, 1 chocolate milk. Optional: ice & straw.
convenience.choco-banana-latte_s1: Pour banana milk first into a cup/bottle. Cold tastes best.
convenience.choco-banana-latte_s2: Add chocolate milk little by little. Start around banana:choco = 2:1, then adjust.
convenience.choco-banana-latte_s3: Shake or stir until even. Add more chocolate milk for a richer cocoa taste.
convenience.choco-banana-latte_tip: It’s quite sweet — adjust gradually. Use an ice cup for a colder drink.
convenience.banana-americanoDesc: Classic mix of banana milk and iced Americano
convenience.banana-americano_pageTitle: How to make Banana milk + iced Americano
convenience.banana-americano_lead: A classic convenience-store drink hack: sweet banana milk plus bitter coffee becomes a dessert-like latte.
convenience.banana-americano_products: Banana milk · iced Americano (cup/can) · optional straw
convenience.banana-americano_s1: Pick cold banana milk and iced Americano.
convenience.banana-americano_s2: Pour coffee into the banana milk little by little. Start with 1/3–1/2 of the coffee, then taste.
convenience.banana-americano_s3: Shake or stir. Add more coffee if too sweet, or keep more milk if too bitter.
convenience.banana-americano_tip: You can also pour banana milk into the coffee cup. Choose low-fat banana milk if you want lighter calories.
convenience.biyottDesc: Popular cup yogurt dessert at convenience stores
convenience.biyott_lead: Biyott is an easy-to-find cup yogurt dessert in Korean convenience stores. Tangy-sweet flavors and many varieties make it a tourist-friendly grab-and-go dessert.
convenience.biyott_what: A refrigerated cup yogurt you eat with a spoon. Flavors include plain, strawberry, peach, and more. Similar products sit together in the dairy/dessert fridge.
convenience.biyott_why: It’s light, sweet, inexpensive, and easy to eat while traveling — a simple post-meal dessert without hunting for a café.
convenience.biyott_tip: Check the fridge section and expiration date. On hot days, eat soon or carry an ice pack. Many flavors are quite sweet — one cup is usually enough.

shopping.intro: From Olive Young and Daiso to duty-free and markets — shopping tips visitors ask about most.
shopping.olive1: Start with ‘Olive Young Picks’ and sale shelves. Sheet masks, sunscreen, and tints are popular gifts.
shopping.olive2: App/membership coupons can add discounts — ask staff about similar items on sale.
shopping.olive3: Airport/Myeongdong stores stock tourist sets; neighborhood stores may differ in stock and price.
shopping.daiso1: Great for fixed-price household goods, stationery, and travel bits that fit a suitcase.
shopping.daiso2: Floors are categorized — follow in-store signs for travel/storage keywords.
shopping.duty1: Downtown/airport duty-free may need passport and flight info — check pickup rules.
shopping.duty2: Shop tax-free needs a minimum spend, passport, and airport refund steps. Look for TAX FREE signs.
shopping.market1: Gwangjang, Namdaemun, and Dongdaemun sometimes prefer cash — ask if cards work.
shopping.market2: Myeongdong, Hongdae, and Gangnam mix brands and street food; weekends get crowded.
